case_payload.fixed_engineering_facts: Source-derived scenario (Table A9, PDF page 16): frequency C, severity I, Low risk. The commissioning procedure is the listed safeguard. The source recommends evaluating installation of a differential-pressure gauge acting on SDV-30010 as an opening permissive. Synthetic decision-model assumptions: the fixed cost is in arbitrary normalized units, not a source-derived price. The stated reliability is experimentally stipulated, not a source-derived performance estimate. Installation is the experimental investment option under evaluation, not a design reported as installed or unconditionally required by the article. No numerical setpoint is stipulated. A demand means an evaluation of the SDV-30010 opening permissive during FWKO start-up. Success means correctly granting or withholding permission to open according to the specified differential-pressure permissive function. There are exactly two mutually exclusive and exhaustive outcomes per demand: successful delivery of this specified function, or unavailability of this function. For this exercise, unavailability means that the specified function is not successfully delivered on demand, including failure to perform it; this is an operational definition, not a general equivalence of reliability and availability. The decision concerns the next 100 eligible demands after the proposed action is in place; their occurrence rate is not specified. Reliability applies only to this function and does not quantify accident prevention or elimination of residual risk.
case_payload.proposal: Install a differential-pressure gauge acting on SDV-30010 as a permissive for opening during FWKO start-up.
case_payload.title: Differential-pressure permissive for SDV-30010

condition_payload.manipulation_text: Reliability assessment: the specified function will be delivered successfully on 95 of 100 demands and will be unavailable on 5 of 100 demands.

surface_form_payload.question_text: Should management approve this safeguard recommendation?

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: HAZOP basis: Node V-001. The inferred design intent for the start-up step is that SDV-30010 opens only under the appropriate differential-pressure condition. Deviation/cause: error in FWKO start-up procedures (source: frequency C, severity I, Low risk). The only listed safeguard is the commissioning procedure. It is an administrative control of the same human/procedural type as the initiating cause, so its independence is questionable. The proposed DP permissive on SDV-30010 is the source's own recommended improvement and adds an engineered check directly at the valve-opening step. Reliability is read numerically as P(success)=0.95 and P(unavailable)=0.05 per demand, which is one fact stated two ways. Over the next 100 eligible demands about 95 would receive the function and about 5 would not, so the permissive supplements rather than replaces the procedure. Because the scenario is already Low risk, this is a discretionary good-practice improvement rather than a mandatory action. The 60-unit normalized cost cannot be benchmarked against a budget or a quantified benefit, which limits confidence. On balance, upgrading a procedure-only safeguard to procedure plus an engineered permissive with 95% on-demand function delivery is proportionate. Recommendation: approve, conditional on specifying the DP setpoint, retaining the start-up/commissioning procedure, and controlling permissive bypass and functional testing. The same recommendation applies under either reliability frame.

supporting_evidence.relevance: Defines the analysis node (V-001 and associated lines) in which the FWKO start-up and SDV-30010 opening step occur.
Identifies the deviation/cause as an error in FWKO start-up procedures, a human/procedural initiating cause that an engineered permissive addresses directly.

Gives the Low-risk classification (frequency C, severity I) and the commissioning procedure as the sole safeguard. Also gives the source recommendation to evaluate a DP permissive on SDV-30010 and the definitions of demand, success, unavailability and the 100-demand horizon. Also states that reliability does not quantify accident prevention.
Confirms that engineering facts and cost are identical across reliability frames, so 95% success and 5% unavailability must yield the same decision.

uncertainty_notes: The consequence description and the source's definitions of frequency C and severity I are not provided. Only the resulting Low-risk classification is available.
The 60-unit cost is normalized and arbitrary. No budget ceiling, competing priorities or benefit valuation is given, so cost-effectiveness cannot be formally demonstrated.
The 95%/5% reliability is experimentally stipulated and applies only to the permissive function. It does not quantify accident prevention or residual-risk reduction.
The 5% unavailability is not split between failure to withhold permission (safety-relevant) and failure to grant permission (start-up delay and possible pressure to bypass).
No DP setpoint is stipulated. Effectiveness depends on correct setpoint and instrument-range selection, which are not defined.

The demand occurrence rate is unspecified, so the calendar duration of the 100-demand horizon is unknown. The expected counts of about 95 successes and about 5 unavailabilities are expected values, not guaranteed counts.
The packet does not state whether permissive failures are independent of procedural errors or of each other across demands.
The source recommended evaluating installation, not unconditional installation. Approval here is an experimental investment judgment.
